Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 108, verses 1–3:

It is related in the narrations that the vagabonds of Quraysh would constantly pursue the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They remained engaged in plots against his call and kept up mockery and ridicule against him. In this way, in their own estimation, they kept the common people from hearing the message of truth that he had brought. The leaders of these vagabonds were 'Aas ibn Wa'il, 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, Abu Lahab, Abu Jahl and others. They used to say that the Prophet (ﷺ) is "abtar," meaning that he has no male offspring. Some of them even advised: "Leave him alone; he has no children. When he dies, this movement will end on its own."

Since male offspring held great importance in Arab society, this propaganda scheme had considerable effect among them. His opponents and enemies encouraged this base propaganda, and it certainly had an impact on the blessed heart of the Prophet (ﷺ). For this reason this surah was revealed, so that the burden on his heart would be lifted, he would feel joy and freshness, the reality of the abundant good with which he had been sent would firmly settle in hearts, and it would be made clear that in truth it is your enemies who are "abtar," and that they are heading toward an end where their roots will be cut off and their name and trace will be erased.

﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾ (1:108). Kawthar derives from kathrah (abundance), and its meaning is limitless and unmeasured. This sense is the exact opposite of what every fool attributed to him; namely, that what We have given you is a great, boundless bounty. It will continue unceasingly, and its chain will never be cut. Whoever reflects on what that abundant bounty is, which Allah gave to His Prophet, can find it; wherever he looks, he will find it present.

First, the office of prophethood that was given to him is abundant good; through it he was connected to the great Truth. He was connected to that great Being besides whom there is no other, namely the Divine Essence, and whoever is connected to the Divine Essence attains everything.

Then this abundant good can also be seen in the form of the Qur'an. Not the whole Qur'an alone, but each and every surah of it is abundant good, and each surah is a fountain whose overflowing bounties never end.

Then the entire higher realm sends blessings and peace upon him, and also upon those who send blessings and peace upon him. Thus his blessed name is joined, throughout this entire universe, with the name of Allah.

Then abundant good also exists in the form of his Sunnah, and this Sunnah is alive and everlasting in every corner of this world. Millions upon millions of people follow his Sunnah, millions upon millions are his devotees, and until the Day of Resurrection millions of human beings will continue to send blessings and peace upon him.

Then this Kawthar also exists in the form of that abundant good from which this entire world has benefited, and these bounties have continued throughout the whole of human history, whether or not people are aware of it, and whether or not they believe. Yet the effects of that fountain have reached them, and in some way or another they have benefited.

In short, this Kawthar is that abundant and great good whose count is not possible. If we, with our limited capacity, try to count it, we will only diminish its worth and value.

In truth it is a Kawthar, and there is no end to its bounties. Its knowledge and insights have no bounds or limits. This is why the Qur'an left it unspecified by calling it Kawthar, and every "good" falls within its scope: good in the highest degree.

Some narrations state that Kawthar is a river in Paradise which was given to the Messenger (ﷺ). Hadrat Ibn 'Abbas (رضي الله عنه) said regarding this that this river too is part of the abundant good that was given to him. Thus Kawthar is a part of al-Kawthar. This is an extremely appropriate reconciliation that can be made on this matter.

﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾ (2:108). After this emphatic mention of the abundant good, which was given to the Prophet (ﷺ) in spite of those in Makkah who spread misleading propaganda against the Islamic movement and plotted against the call of Islam, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is directed to thank Allah for the bestowal of that abundant good. The first thanks owed to Allah is that a person, in worship and in all acts of drawing near, turns solely to Allah, the One without partner, and remembers Him alone: in prayer and in sacrifice. Prayer should be purely for Allah, and sacrifice should be purely for Allah.

﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾ (2:108): that is, pray to Allah alone and sacrifice in the name of Allah alone. Do not care about the mischief of those who associate partners with Allah; worship Allah, do not join others with Him in worship, and do not mention any other name than Allah's over the sacrifice of Allah.

The Qur'an repeatedly points to the fact that over all slaughtered animals only Allah's name is to be pronounced; that animals over which Allah's name has been mentioned are lawful as a matter of principle, while those over which Allah's name has not been mentioned are forbidden to eat. The reason is that the Qur'an seeks to purify human life from every kind of traces and traces of shirk. Purifying belief from shirk alone is not the aim of Islam; rather, the Qur'an negates shirk from the whole of human life, negating it in all its meanings and concepts, because this is a religion of unity and Tawhid, and its doctrine of Tawhid is complete from every aspect. Therefore this religion pursues shirk until the last breath and erases its marks from all its manifestations. The Qur'an pursues shirk to such a distance that it does not let it take refuge in any hiding place. It eradicates it from human psychology, human conscience and human thought. It wipes it out from Islamic worship. It removes it from the customs and traditions of human life, because life is an interconnected whole (a system) and cannot be cut into pieces and fragments. Therefore Islam eliminates the effects of shirk from the whole of human life and turns the entire direction of life toward Allah alone, making it fully clear, pure and clean, whether the matter concerns sacrifices and slaughter, worship, belief, or rites and customs.

﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾ (3:108). The verdict of the first verse was that your root has not been cut; rather, you are the possessor of al-Kawthar. In this verse, the hunter is caught in his own trap: Muhammad (ﷺ) is not "abtar," but the roots of your enemies have been cut, and those who dislike you are destined to have their name and trace wiped out.

And this threat of Allah proved true: those people's name and trace were erased. From this world their very mention came to an end, while the name of Muhammad (ﷺ) was raised high and his ranks continue to be recited. Today, after fifteen hundred years, we see that the prophecy made in this verse has come true, and the fulfilment of this verse is before us today in a clear form, which was not so evident to those who first heard these verses.

The truth is that the root of faith, truth and goodness can never be cut. The roots of these things are deep in the earth, and their branches spread far into the atmosphere of the heavens. Rather, the root of disbelief, falsehood and evil is cut, even if it appears outwardly fresh and flourishing.

The fact is that Allah's standard differs from the standard of human beings. Humans are deceived; they are caught by illusion and begin to think that their standards really determine realities. The example given in this surah is a perpetual and everlasting example for us. Just consider: where are those people who used such base language about Muhammad (ﷺ), and who thought that they had misled the masses, that the religion of Muhammad (ﷺ) had come to an end, and that its path had been blocked? The question is, where are they now? Where is their mention, where are their traces? In contrast, Muhammad (ﷺ), whom they called "abtar," has been granted abundant good in every respect.

The truth is that it is impossible for the call to Allah, the movement of truth and goodness, to come to an end and have its root cut. Nor can the callers of this movement be "abtar," because the originator of this movement is ever-living, enduring, everlasting and eternal. Rather, disbelief, falsehood and evil are destined to end, and the trace of their bearers is destined to be erased, even though for a short period these things may appear firm and everlasting, and their roots may appear to spread far. This is the true word that Allah declares, and what the plotters and deceivers said was falsehood, is falsehood, and will forever remain falsehood.
